quickSummary: Matter consists of fundamental subatomic particles: Electrons (Thomson, 1897), Protons (Goldstein, 1886), and Neutrons (Chadwick, 1932). Rutherford's gold foil experiment revealed the dense, positively charged nucleus with dimensions R = R₀ A^(1/3).
summary: Master fundamental subatomic particle properties, isotopic classification (isodiaphers, isosteres), and Rutherford scattering mathematics.

summaryBox.title: Subatomic Particles Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Electron: e/m = 1.7588 × 10¹¹ C/kg (gas invariant); Proton: e/m varies with gas; Neutron: Chadwick nuclear reaction ⁹₄Be + ⁴₂He → ¹²₆C + ¹₀n.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
SUBATOMIC PARTICLES MATRIX
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                             ▼                             ▼
  ELECTRON (e⁻)                 PROTON (p⁺)                 NEUTRON (n⁰)
  ├── J.J. Thomson (1897)        ├── E. Goldstein (1886)      ├── James Chadwick (1932)
  ├── e/m = 1.7588 × 10¹¹ C/kg   ├── e/m depends on gas       ├── Alpha bombardment on Be
  └── m_e = 9.10938 × 10⁻³¹ kg   └── m_p = 1.67262 × 10⁻²⁷ kg └── m_n = 1.67493 × 10⁻²⁷ kg
conceptBreakdown.content:
Atoms are built from three fundamental subatomic particles:

1. **Electron ($e^-$ / $\beta^-$)**: Discovered by J.J. Thomson (1897) in cathode ray discharge tubes. Specific charge $\frac{e}{m_e} = 1.7588 \times 10^{11}\text{ C/kg}$ is constant regardless of cathode material or residual gas. Absolute mass $m_e = 9.109383 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg} = 0.00054857\text{ u}$. Absolute charge $-1.602176 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$.

2. **Proton ($p^+$ / $^1_1\text{H}^+$)**: Discovered in perforated cathode tubes (Canal/Anode rays) by E. Goldstein (1886), characterized by Rutherford (1919). $\frac{e}{m}$ depends on the residual gas and is maximum for Hydrogen gas. Absolute mass $m_p = 1.672622 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg} = 1.007276\text{ u}$. Absolute charge $+1.602176 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$.

3. **Neutron ($n^0$ / $^1_0\text{n}$)**: Discovered by James Chadwick (1932) by bombarding a Beryllium target with high-speed $\alpha$-particles:

$$^{9}_{4}\text{Be} + ^{4}_{2}\text{He} \longrightarrow ^{12}_{6}\text{C} + ^{1}_{0}\text{n}$$

Neutral charge ($0\text{ C}$), absolute mass $m_n = 1.674927 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg} = 1.008665\text{ u}$ (slightly heavier than a proton).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.2 Atomic Terminology & Isotopic Classification
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.2 Atomic Terminology & Isotopic Classification
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Atomic Number ($Z$)**: Total nuclear protons ($Z = p = e^-$ in neutral atom).
• **Mass Number ($A$)**: Total nucleons ($A = Z + N$).
• **Isotopes**: Same $Z$, different $A$ ($^1_1\text{H}, ^2_1\text{H}, ^3_1\text{H}$).
• **Isobars**: Same $A$, different $Z$ ($^{40}_{18}\text{Ar}, ^{40}_{19}\text{K}, ^{40}_{20}\text{Ca}$).
• **Isotones**: Identical neutrons $N = A - Z$ ($^{14}_6\text{C}, ^{15}_7\text{N}, ^{16}_8\text{O}$ where $N = 8$).
• **Isodiaphers**: Identical neutron excess $N - Z = A - 2Z$ ($^{238}_{92}\text{U}$ and $^{234}_{90}\text{Th}$ where $N - Z = 54$).
• **Isoelectronic Species**: Equal total electrons ($\text{N}^{3-}, \text{O}^{2-}, \text{F}^-, \text{Ne}, \text{Na}^+, \text{Mg}^{2+}, \text{Al}^{3+}$ all have $10\ e^-$).
• **Isosteres**: Molecules with same number of atoms AND same number of electrons ($\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ both have 3 atoms and 22 electrons).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.3 Rutherford α-Scattering & Nuclear Dimensions
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.3 Rutherford α-Scattering & Nuclear Dimensions
conceptBreakdown.content:
Bombardment of thin Gold foil ($400\text{ nm}$) with $^{4}_{2}\text{He}^{2+}$ $\alpha$-particles showed:
1. Most $\alpha$-particles pass undeflected $\implies$ Atom is mostly empty space.
2. Few deflected at large angles $\implies$ Positive charge concentrated in tiny region.
3. 1 in 20,000 recoils at $\approx 180^\circ$ $\implies$ Dense, massive nucleus at center.

• **Scattering Distribution**: $N(\theta) \propto \frac{1}{\sin^4(\theta/2)}$.

• **Distance of Closest Approach ($r_0$)**: Kinetic energy equals electrostatic potential energy at reversal:

$$E_k = \frac{1}{2}m_\alpha v^2 = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{(2e)(Ze)}{r_0} \implies \mathbf{r_0 = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{2Ze^2}{E_k}}$$

• **Nuclear Radius ($R$)**: $\mathbf{R = R_0 A^{1/3}}$ where $R_0 \approx 1.2\text{--}1.4 \times 10^{-15}\text{ m}$ ($1.2\text{--}1.4\text{ fm}$) and $A$ is the Mass Number.

• **Classical Collapse Failure**: Accelerating electrons must continuously radiate electromagnetic energy (Maxwell electrodynamics), spiraling into the nucleus within $\approx 10^{-8}\text{ s}$. Rutherford's model also failed to explain discrete atomic line spectra.

quickRevision: Chadwick discovered neutron via ⁹₄Be + ⁴₂He → ¹²₆C + ¹₀n.
Isodiaphers have identical N - Z = A - 2Z.
Isosteres have identical atom counts and electron counts.
Distance of closest approach r₀ = (1/4πε₀) · (2Ze² / E_k).
Nuclear radius R = R₀ · A^(1/3) where R₀ ≈ 1.2–1.4 fm.
